feature_results.rationale: This is a new taxonomy feature with no prior research pass for Claude Code, evaluated fresh against the has_criteria: 'Documentation describes admin-accessible audit log events or a usage-metrics API/report covering the tool's access or configuration.' Two official, org/admin-facing mechanisms cover Claude Code: (1) the Compliance API exposes a queryable, organization-wide activity feed of admin/system events (membership changes, API key creation, account setting updates) retained for 6 years, giving admins programmatic access to per-event audit logs; and (2) the Claude Code Analytics API/dashboard reports aggregated usage metrics specific to Claude Code (sessions, lines of code added/removed, commits, and pull requests) for organization admins, and Claude Code also supports exporting live usage telemetry via OpenTelemetry. Together these exceed the exclusion (personal, client-side-only activity history) and meet has_criteria for organization/administrator-facing audit logging and usage metrics.

evidence.excerpt: The Compliance API provides an activity feed that logs security-relevant events across your organization.
The API currently tracks admin and system activities—actions that modify access or configuration of resources, like adding a member to a workspace, creating an API key, updating account settings.

The Claude Code Analytics Admin API provides programmatic access to daily aggregated usage metrics for Claude Code users, enabling organizations to analyze developer productivity and build custom dashboards.

constraints.description: The Compliance API must be enabled per organization by an Anthropic account team, and the Claude Code Analytics Admin API is unavailable for individual (non-organizational) accounts; both are organization/admin-level features, not available to personal consumer accounts.

The Compliance API's activity feed logs admin/system actions that change access or configuration; it explicitly does not log inference activity such as user prompts or model conversation content, so it does not provide a transcript-level audit trail of chat/agent content.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code ships a first-party "Code Review" capability (currently in research preview) that analyzes GitHub pull requests and automatically posts inline review comments identifying logic errors, security vulnerabilities, and regressions, driven by a fleet of specialized agents examining the diff in the context of the full codebase. Repos can be tuned via a REVIEW.md file whose contents are injected as the highest-priority instruction block for the review pipeline. This meets the has_criteria of a documented, dedicated automated diff/PR review workflow producing comments/suggestions; the previous profile's 'has' rating is confirmed, with an added note that the feature is gated by plan and release stage.

evidence.excerpt: Code Review analyzes GitHub pull requests and posts findings as inline comments on the lines of code where it found issues. A fleet of specialized agents examine the code changes in the context of your full codebase, looking for logic errors, security vulnerabilities, broken edge cases, and subtle regressions.
The contents of REVIEW.md are injected into the system prompt of every agent in the review pipeline as the highest-priority instruction block, taking precedence over the default review guidance.

constraints.description: Code Review is available for Team and Enterprise subscriptions only, and is not available for organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled.
Code Review is in research preview.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code's own documentation states its default/native code-discovery mechanism is 'agentic search': it traverses the filesystem and uses grep to find what it needs, explicitly without requiring a codebase index to be built, maintained, or uploaded, and vendor guidance frames semantic (embedding-based) search as an optional add-on to consider only if agentic search is insufficient - not the built-in mechanism. Whole-repository, natural-language, meaning-based (embedding/vector) search is available, but only by installing a third-party MCP plugin such as Sourcegraph (semantic search, symbol navigation, Deep Search) or Greptile (natural-language codebase queries). Because native, out-of-the-box semantic search is not the documented default and requires an additional integration, this is a partial rather than a full match to the has_criteria, consistent with the previous profile's 'partial' rating.

evidence.excerpt: it traverses the file system, reads files, uses grep to find exactly what it needs, and follows references across the codebase. It operates locally on the developer's machine and doesn't require a codebase index to be built, maintained, or uploaded to a server.

connects to your Sourcegraph instance via MCP, giving you access to semantic search, keyword/regex search, commit and diff history, symbol navigation, reference tracing, and Sourcegraph's Deep Search.

constraints.description: Native Claude Code search is grep/glob-based agentic search, not embedding-based semantic search; project-wide, meaning-based semantic search requires installing a third-party MCP plugin such as Sourcegraph or Greptile.

feature_results.rationale: Re-research, with particular attention to whether IDE extensions added inline suggestion behavior since the last pass, finds no change: no official Anthropic source describes as-you-type ghost-text or inline code suggestions generated in an editor without an explicit prompt. Claude Code's overview and product positioning still frame it as an instruction-driven agentic tool rather than an autocomplete assistant. Current (July 2026) documentation and changelog content show only command-UI autocomplete conveniences (slash-command autocomplete, @-mention/file-path autocomplete, shell history tab completion, an emoji-shortcode autocomplete added to the prompt input) -- none of these complete source code inline as the developer types it, which this feature explicitly requires. The official pricing page (claude.com/pricing) was also checked: its per-plan feature lists (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) cover usage limits, model access, context window, SSO/SCIM/RBAC and admin controls, with no mention of inline code completion, autocomplete, or ghost-text suggestions as a plan-gated capability on any tier -- this is consistent with the feature simply not existing rather than being gated behind a plan. A still-open community feature request on the product's own GitHub repository ('Feature request: Inline/tab code completions in VS Code and JetBrains extensions') further corroborates that ghost-text/inline tab completion in the VS Code and JetBrains extensions remains unimplemented as of this pass; per protocol this non-official issue tracker item is used only to corroborate the absence, not as the basis for the status itself, which rests on the official documentation, changelog, and pricing pages showing no such feature. Documentation, product page, changelog, and pricing source classes were all checked with no supporting statement for inline completion.

feature_results.rationale: This is a new taxonomy feature with no prior research pass for Claude Code. The Claude Code 'Legal and compliance' documentation confirms that a customer's existing commercial agreement (Claude API direct, or via Amazon Bedrock/Google Cloud) applies to Claude Code usage, and Anthropic's commercial/API terms include a stated IP indemnification commitment: Anthropic will defend commercial customers against third-party copyright-infringement claims arising from authorized use of the service or its outputs and will pay approved settlements or judgments, subject to standard carve-outs (customer modifications to outputs, combination with other technology, customer-supplied inputs, knowingly infringing use, patents, certain trademark claims). This satisfies the indemnification half of the has_criteria for eligible commercial/enterprise agreements. However, no official Claude Code or Anthropic documentation was found describing a configurable, customer-facing filter that blocks code suggestions matching public code (an analogue to GitHub Copilot's public-code duplication filter); the dedicated Claude Code legal-and-compliance page covers commercial-agreement applicability, BAA/Zero Data Retention extension, and the Usage Policy, with no mention of a duplication/matching-code control. Per partial_criteria ('only one of the two... is documented'), the correct status is partial rather than has.

evidence.excerpt: Whether you're using Claude API directly (1P) or through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform (3P), your existing commercial agreement will apply to Claude Code usage, unless you've mutually agreed otherwise.

Anthropic will defend customers from any copyright infringement claim made against them for their authorized use of the services or outputs, and will pay for any approved settlements or judgments that result.

constraints.description: The IP indemnification commitment is provided under Anthropic's commercial/API terms of service (e.g. direct API, Bedrock, Vertex commercial agreements) that Claude Code usage falls under; it is not stated for free/Pro consumer terms.

Indemnification does not apply where the claim arises from customer modifications to outputs, combination with non-Anthropic technology, customer-supplied prompts/inputs, use the customer knew or should have known was infringing, practice of a patented invention, or certain trademark claims.

No configurable public-code/duplication-matching suggestion filter is documented for Claude Code; the dedicated legal-and-compliance documentation page covers commercial-agreement scope, BAA/ZDR, and Usage Policy only.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code documents both a dedicated large-codebase/monorepo setup mechanism and explicit context-window handling: recent models (e.g. Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 5) support a 1M-token context window on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plans, and when the window nears its hard cutoff the in-progress task is automatically summarized so work continues in a new context window. Official guidance also recommends scoping work (layered root/subdirectory CLAUDE.md files, on-demand skills, starting in subdirectories rather than the repo root) specifically to keep large repositories usable. This confirms the previous profile's 'has' rating.

evidence.excerpt: When using Claude Code with Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plans, Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 5, and other recent models support a 1M token context window.
Context windows are a hard cutoff, so when nearing the end, the task being worked on is automatically summarized into a smaller description and the model continues in a new context window.
Claude Code works best when scoped to the part of the codebase that's actually relevant to the task, starting in subdirectories rather than at the repo root.

constraints.description: The 1M-token context window is limited to recent models (e.g. Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 5) and to Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plans.

Anthropic now documents a dedicated official mobile experience for Claude Code that is distinct from a mobile browser view of the web app: the 'Claude Code on mobile' page (code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile) describes the official Claude app for iOS and Android (distributed through the App Store and Google Play) as a client that lets a user start, monitor, and steer Claude Code coding sessions directly from their phone. feature_results.rationale: Official documentation still describes subagents as separate agent instances that the main Claude Code agent can spawn to handle focused subtasks in their own context windows, with automatic or explicit delegation and support for running several subagents concurrently. A dedicated 'Run agents in parallel' documentation page (distinct from the subagents reference) further documents supported patterns for coordinating multiple agent instances (parallel sessions via worktrees, agent teams, forked subagents that inherit context via /subtask). This is a documented, supported delegation mechanism, satisfying the has_criteria. Note: some third-party (non-official) community write-ups disagree on whether a subagent can itself spawn further subagents (nested delegation); since this is not corroborated by an official source and is not central to the has_criteria (which only requires documented delegation to subagents/parallel instances), it is not treated as a conflict against the feature's status, only noted as an open, unofficial discrepancy.

evidence.excerpt: Subagents are separate agent instances that your main agent can spawn to handle focused subtasks.
You can use them to isolate context, run multiple analyses in parallel, and apply specialized instructions without adding to the main agent's prompt.

feature_results.rationale: Re-verified against current official documentation; the previous 'has' rating still holds and the deployment options have expanded. Claude Code's enterprise deployment documentation confirms enterprise customers can run Claude Code against models hosted in their own Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI instances, and Claude Code now additionally documents a dedicated Microsoft Foundry deployment path (configured via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY and an Azure resource name), plus a 'Claude apps gateway' for routing Claude Code through a self-hosted gateway across Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry with organization SSO and telemetry. This remains a customer-cloud/BYOC deployment within the customer's own account and network boundary rather than the vendor's shared multi-tenant SaaS cloud, satisfying has_criteria. As before, this is not a fully air-gapped, vendor-independent on-premises hosting of model weights.

evidence.excerpt: Enterprise users can run Claude Code using models in existing Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI instances.
Claude Code on Microsoft Foundry can be enabled by setting environment variables including CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1 and providing the Azure resource name through ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE.

The Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry deployment paths are documented for enterprise users/organizations.

Unlike Bedrock and Vertex, Microsoft Foundry has no interactive setup wizard or startup model-availability check, so configuration relies entirely on environment variables and default model aliases can lag the newest release.
